Operating expenses increased $1,830 in the nine months ended September 30, 2026, as compared to the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The net increase was primarily from extraordinary maintenance and repair expenses of $2,055, partially offset by reduced compensation and research and development expenses.

nonint.heading: Operating Expenses
nonint.text: Operating expenses increased $509 in the three months ended September 30, 2026, as compared to the three months ended September 30, 2025. The net increase was primarily from additional extraordinary maintenance and repair expenditures of $157 related to Winter Storm Fern and a facility fire in earlier periods and increased compensation expenses of $99. Operating expenses increased $1,830 in the nine months ended September 30, 2026, as compared to the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The net increase was primarily from extraordinary maintenance and repair expenses of $2,055, partially offset by reduced compensation and research and development expenses.

nonop.heading: Other Income, net
nonop.text: Other income, net decreased $245 in the three months ended September 30, 2026, as compared to the same period of 2025, partially from a reduction in interest income. In the current three-month period interest income was $166 as compared to $1,012 in the prior period. Other income, net decreased $2,536 in the nine months ended September 30, 2026, as compared to the same period of 2025 primarily from the reduction in interest income. In the current nine-month period interest income was $673 as compared to $3,317 in the prior period.

tax.text: The effective tax rate for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, was 3.8% and 1.4%, respectively, compared to (1.8%) and (0.4%) for the same periods in 2025. For both periods, the effective tax rate differed from the U.S. federal statutory rate of 21% primarily due to the impact of the valuation allowance recorded against the Company's deferred tax assets. For the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026, the effective tax rate was also impacted by a discrete income tax benefit of $423 recorded in the third quarter of 2026 resulting from a reduction in the Company's valuation allowance. For the three and nine months ended September 30, 2025, the effective tax rate also reflected the decrease in the Company’s net deferred tax liability and immaterial state taxes and other items. The discrete income tax benefit of $423 recorded in the third quarter of 2026 relates to the Company’s election out of bonus depreciation for assets placed in service in 2025. During the third quarter of 2026, after the issuance of its 2025 consolidated financial statements, the Company decided to elect out of bonus depreciation under IRC § 168(k) for all applicable asset classes placed in service in 2025 on its 2025 federal income tax return.

ocf.heading: Operating Activities
ocf.text: Cash used in operating activities was $11,477 in the nine months ended September 30, 2026, as compared to $1,299 in the same period of 2025. This increase in cash used was primarily attributable to the change in accounts receivable, including accounts receivable - related parties resulting in a cash outflow of $27,165, the change in inventory of $22,567, and the change in other assets of $8,762. T he Company recognized $13,807 of 2026 production tax credits that had not yet been monetized during the nine months ended September 30, 2026. The Company expects to monetize those credits at fiscal year-end. Also contributing to the current period’s increase in cash used was the change in accrued expenses and other current liabilities of $1,756 and the change in deferred revenue of $786. Partially offsetting these cash outflows was the change in net income of $23,842, the change in accounts payable, including accounts payable - related parties, resulting in a cash inflow of $14,227, and the change in other noncurrent liabilities of $12,036 , $12,500 of which was from a customer payment related to plant expansion. This payment supports the associated customer project and should be distinguished from recurring operating cash generation.

da.text: Adjusted EBITDA allows our chief operating decision maker to assess the performance and liquidity of our business on a consolidated basis to assess the ability of our operating segments to produce operating cash flow to fund working capital needs, to fund capital expenditures, and to pay dividends. In particular, our management believes that adjusted EBITDA permits a comparative assessment of our operating performance and liquidity, relative to performance and liquidity based on GAAP results. This measure isolates the effects of certain items, including depreciation and amortization (which may vary among our operating segments without any correlation to their underlying operating performance), non-cash stock-based compensation expense (which is a non-cash expense that varies widely among similar companies), and non-cash gains and losses on derivative instruments (which can cause net income to appear volatile from period to period relative to the sale of the underlying physical product).

net sales.heading: Revenue Recognition
net sales.text:
The Company recognizes revenue under ASC Topic 606, Revenue from Contracts with Customers. Certain long-term contracts had upfront non-cancellable payments considered material rights. The Company applied the renewal option approach in allocating the transaction price to the material rights. For each of these contracts, the Company estimated the expected contractual volumes to be sold at the most likely expected sales price as a basis for allocating the transaction price to the material right. Estimated amortization is updated quarterly on a prospective basis. These custom chemical contracts have payment terms of 30 days. See Note 3 to our consolidated financial statements for additional information.

For most product sales, revenue is recognized when product is shipped from our facilities and risk of loss and title have passed to the customer, which is in accordance with our customer contracts and the stated shipping terms. Nearly all custom manufactured products are manufactured under written master service agreements. Performance chemicals and biodiesel are generally sold pursuant to the terms of written purchase orders. In general, customers do not have any rights of return, except for quality disputes.

intro.text: FutureFuel is a leading manufacturer of diversified chemical products and biofuels. FutureFuel's chemicals segment manufactures specialty chemicals for specific customers ("custom chemicals") as well as multi-customer specialty chemicals ("performance chemicals"). FutureFuel's custom manufacturing product portfolio includes proprietary agrochemicals, adhesion promoters, a biocide intermediate, and an antioxidant precursor. FutureFuel's performance chemicals products include a portfolio of proprietary nylon and polyester polymer modifiers and several small-volume specialty chemicals and solvents for diverse applications. FutureFuel's biofuels segment primarily produces and sells biodiesel to its customers. Please visit www.futurefuelcorporation.com for more information.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Short-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for the cash they will return: financial.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

The nature of our Chemicals segment revenue, which is primarily derived from long-term custom manufacturing agreements, relies on a collaborative planning model rather than a traditional order-book system.

Natural disasters, changes in laws or regulations, trade disputes, war or other outbreak of hostilities, or other political factors in any of the countries or regions in which we operate or do business, or in countries or regions that are key suppliers of strategic raw materials, could negatively impact our competitive position and our ability to maintain market share.

In addition, inflation, natural disasters, changes in laws or regulations, war or other outbreak of hostilities, or other political factors in any of the countries or regions in which we operate or do business, or in countries or regions that are key suppliers of strategic raw materials, could affect availability and costs of raw materials.
The availability of a ready market for biodiesel depends on a number of factors, including the demand for and supply of biodiesel and the proximity of the plant to trucking and terminal facilities.
Growth in the biodiesel industry depends on substantial development of infrastructure for the distribution of biodiesel.
Furthermore, many of our manufacturing control systems rely on legacy hardware and software that may no longer be supported by original equipment manufacturers.
We depend on key personnel, the loss of any of whom could materially adversely affect our future operations.
We depend on our ability to maintain relationships with industry participants, including our strategic partners.

Our ability to maintain commercial arrangements with chemical and biodiesel customers, raw material and feedstock suppliers, and transportation and logistics services providers may depend on maintaining close working relationships with industry participants.
